title: Helpmate: safe shortflow runner for first-line support
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Problem: First-line support repeatedly executes a small set of operational flows (eg. token resets, cache clears, instance reboots) using ad-hoc scripts or copy/paste runbooks. This is slow, error-prone, and produces poor audit trails.

Objective: Build Helpmate — a lightweight, auditable shortflow runner surfaced in the Console and CLI that lets support engineers execute vetted runbooks-as-tasks safely. Key goals: safe-by-default execution (dry-run, approvals), per-step idempotency, granular RBAC, structured telemetry for SLO/latency/cost, and immediate rollback/fallback hooks.

Scope:
- Minimal server-side task runner service that executes typed step primitives (api-call, k8s-rollout, cache-flush, db-query with read-only guard).
- Console UI affordance to select a shortflow, run dry-run, request approval, or execute with a short justification.
- CLI parity for scripted support workflows.
- Audit logs, per-step status, and automated telemetry events that feed into the existing ops-dashboard.
- Integrations: GitHub link to the vetted runbook source (markdown + typed inputs), KMS for ephemeral credentials, and Redwood SSO for RBAC checks.

Non-goals for this ticket: full runbook composer, long-running saga orchestration, or arbitrary shell execution. Those remain for follow-up tickets.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Support can choose a vetted shortflow in Console and run a dry-run that simulates steps without side effects (UI shows simulated outputs).
2) Execution requires appropriate RBAC; users without permission see a clear CTA to request approval.
3) Each executed invocation emits structured telemetry events (start, step.success, step.fail, total.duration, cost-estimate) to ops-dashboard (sample events documented).
4) All executions are recorded in audit logs with user, justification, inputs, and step outputs; logs are queryable via admin logs view.
5) Cancellation/rollback: if a step marked reversible fails, Helpmate triggers the configured rollback primitive and records the result.
6) CLI parity: same dry-run and execute semantics available via helpmate CLI v0.1.
7) Unit/integration tests cover RBAC gating, dry-run semantics, and the three canonical primitives (api-call, k8s-rollout, cache-flush).
implementation_notes:
Plan: 3-week scoped deliverable split into milestones.
- Week 1: lightweight task-runner prototype + primitives library + audit schema.
- Week 2: Console UI for selecting shortflows and dry-run visualization; CLI shim.
- Week 3: RBAC integration, telemetry hooks, rollout and smoke tests; docs.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- We'll restrict primitive set initially to avoid arbitrary shell execution. That minimizes blast radius and eases security review.
- Dry-run will use a mock execution layer that calls sandboxed read-only paths where available and returns synthetic outputs for external systems.
- For latency-sensitive primitives, we'll emit cost-estimates (tokens/compute) but defer automatic batching/optimization to Optimize team follow-up.

Artifacts: Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Helpmate+Shortflow+Spec
Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-helpmate/pull/12
Telemetry schema draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/telemetry/helpmate-events.md
qa_plan: QA steps: create a QA org with two test users (support+viewer), seed three shortflows (token-reset, cache-clear, pod-restart). Verify dry-run shows no side effects by asserting metrics unchanged. Validate RBAC: viewer must be blocked from execute path and can request approval. Execute a shortflow that has a reversible step and force a failure to ensure rollback is triggered and logged. Run integration tests against staging cluster using test credentials. Load test: simulate 100 parallel dry-runs and 10 parallel executes to ensure task-runner remains responsive. Document troubleshooting steps in the PR description.
